result:
The structure is disordered, and I submitted a model that includes it. The puckered ring carbon C7 in the S2 tetrahydrothiophene ring (S2–C5–C6–C7–C9) sits in two positions, as an envelope flap flipping. The evidence was a 2.74 e/Å³ difference peak 1.0 Å from C7, about 1.5 Å from both C9 and C6, plus C7's ADP being clearly larger than the other ring atoms'. Every other peak was under 0.95 e/Å³ and sat next to Br or Cu, so I read those as heavy-atom noise, not disorder.

I split C7 into C7 (PART 1) and C7B (PART 2), with occupancies tied to a free variable that refined to 0.755/0.245. I added SADI on the C6–C7/C7B and C7/C7B–C9 bonds and RIGU/SIMU on the ring atoms involved. The hydrogens on the neighbouring C6 and C9 are split by part. R1 fell from 0.0328 to 0.0297, wR2 from 0.083 to 0.075 and GooF from 1.20 to 1.09. The peak at C7 is gone, and the largest remaining peak (0.90 e/Å³) is near Br1.

One compromise: the refinement engine wouldn't let PART 2 hydrogens ride on C6 and C9, which are shared by both parts. I calculated their ideal positions by hand and fixed them there instead, so those 4 hydrogens won't follow any later shifts of their carbons. All other hydrogens, including the ones on C7B, ride normally.
